title: Switch port shut down by port security
symptom: A desk lost its network after the user plugged in a small personal switch
user_description: I brought a little network switch from home so I could plug in my laptop and the PC at the same time. Now neither works and the wall port seems dead.

options.text: Keep trying the other wall ports until one works
options.why: The same rule will shut those ports too, and the cause is still plugged in.

options.text: Plug his switch into a different port instead
options.why: Personal network devices are not allowed and would just trigger the same protection.

options.text: Unplug the switch in the server room to reset it
options.why: Cuts off everyone connected to it and does not undo the port shutdown.

options.text: Remove the personal switch, explain the rule, and escalate to the network team so they can re-enable the port
options.why: Port security shuts a port when unknown devices appear on it. The device must go, and only the network team can turn the port back on.

hints: What changed at this desk just before it stopped?
Why might a company block extra devices on a port?
Who can turn a shut-down switch port back on?
real_world_tip: If he needs two devices at the desk, raise a request for a second port or a dock. Never let users add their own network gear.

escalation.team_why: The switch is run by the network team. Only they can check the port and switch it back on.

details.text: The desk and wall port number
details.why: Tells them exactly which switch port to check.

details.text: What was plugged in (a small personal network switch)
details.why: Explains why the port shut down, so they know it was not a fault.
Helps them find the event in the switch logs.

details.text: That the personal switch has been removed
details.why: They should only re-enable the port once the cause is gone.

details.text: Ask them to turn off port security for this desk
details.why: Port security protects the network. Turning it off for convenience would leave a gap.
